nameStory: The little floatingheart gets its charming name from its heart-shaped leaves that bob on the water's surface like tiny green valentines. The 'little' part distinguishes it from other floating plants with similar leaves, while 'floatingheart' perfectly captures how these adorable leaf hearts seem to dance on quiet pond waters.
description: Little floatingheart is a delicate aquatic plant that creates carpets of small, heart-shaped leaves floating on the surface of quiet waters. The leaves are typically 1-3 inches across and emerge from underwater stems rooted in the muddy bottom. In summer, tiny white flowers with fringed petals peek up just above the water surface, giving the plant an almost fairy-like appearance. It's a petite member of the water plant community, never overwhelming but always eye-catching.

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Perfect heart-shaped leaves that float flat on the water surface, glossy green on top and often purplish underneath, feeling smooth and slightly waxy to the touch

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Tiny white flowers about half an inch across with five delicately fringed petals that look almost lacy, rising just above the water on short stems

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Forms floating mats or scattered patches with leaves connected by slender underwater stems, never fully submerged but rooted in bottom mud

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Leaves have a deep notch where they attach to the stem, creating that classic valentine heart shape with rounded lobes

habitat: Look for little floatingheart in quiet, shallow waters of ponds, slow-moving streams, and protected coves of lakes throughout New England. It prefers soft, muddy bottoms in waters 1-6 feet deep and thrives in areas with some protection from strong currents or wave action. You'll often find it growing alongside other aquatic plants like water lilies and pondweeds.

seasonality.spring: New heart-shaped leaves begin emerging and floating to the surface as water warms, creating fresh green patches on previously empty water.
seasonality.summer: Peak growing season with full leaf displays and delicate white flowers blooming from July through August, creating the most beautiful floating carpets.
seasonality.fall: Leaves may persist into early fall but begin to yellow and sink as temperatures drop, with the plant preparing to overwinter from underwater roots.
seasonality.winter: Completely absent from the surface with all above-water parts died back, surviving as dormant roots and stems buried in bottom sediments.

funFact: Little floatingheart can actually 'walk' across a pond over time by sending out underwater runners that pop up new heart-shaped leaves in different spots, essentially allowing the plant to migrate to better growing conditions without anyone noticing!
confusionNotes: Most commonly confused with small water lily leaves, but floatingheart leaves are much smaller, perfectly heart-shaped with that telltale notch, and feel thinner and more delicate. Water lily leaves are rounder, thicker, and often have a pie-slice notch rather than a heart-shaped one.
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called 'little floatingheart,' this plant belongs to the bogbean family, not a lily family as its appearance might suggest. The bogbean family includes mostly wetland plants, and this aquatic lifestyle makes little floatingheart quite unique among its mostly bog-dwelling relatives.
compareHints: Little floatingheart differs from its cousin water fringe by having much smaller, more perfectly heart-shaped leaves and tinier flowers. Water fringe has larger, rounder leaves that can be 2-4 inches across and showier yellow flowers, while little floatingheart keeps everything dainty and white. Think of little floatingheart as the delicate miniature version of the floating plant family.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Water fringe differs from its close relative little floatingheart primarily in flower color and size - little floatingheart has smaller white flowers instead of the bright yellow fringed blooms of water fringe.
